fatal_errors: The proposed cryo-rolling and partial-recrystallization route does not reconstruct the target 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2 h HPHT treatment.
The hypothesis does not predict the target transformation from incoherent FCC/B2 lamellae into a coherent hierarchically patterned interface structure.
The proposed HDI/back-stress mechanism replaces the target mechanism of preferential FCC-to-B2 dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces.

The predicted ductility of 12–14% is far below the target uniform elongation of approximately 36%, and the proposed validation does not test the target phase-wise GND-density convergence or distributed-microcracking signature.
explanation: This is a scientifically credible alternative strategy rather than a reconstruction of the hidden result. The cited studies directly support heterogeneous-grain, cryo-rolling, partial-recrystallization, and precipitation approaches that can improve strength and ductility in selected medium- and high-entropy alloys. The proposed controls, EBSD/TEM, strain-hardening measurements, and loading-unloading-reloading tests could discriminate HDI hardening from homogeneous recrystallization. However, the answer shifts among materially distinct alloy systems and makes coherent nanoprecipitates optional, so not every claimed mediator applies to the stated eutectic alloy. It also does not isolate cryo-rolling from conventional rolling with an otherwise identical partial anneal. Most importantly, it misses the defining HPHT conditions, coherent FCC/B2 interface evolution, interphase dislocation-transfer mechanism, approximately 36% ductility, fracture-mode transition, and phase-resolved GND convergence of the target paper. Novelty is limited because the route closely synthesizes already demonstrated approaches in E1–E4.
